dimensions.note: The monograph's thesis (section 2) is that Fumiya transfers an already existing gaming learning ethic into unfamiliar domains and then has to revise who selects a goal, who bears its cost and who has authority over another person's end. Section 5 states conditional tendencies (mechanism-first attention, uneven learning, the difference between an informative loss and a disqualifying one, a revisable goal hierarchy, action as both resource and escape, sincerity with unstable jurisdiction). Section 6 keeps competence, confidence, status, self-concept, agency and values separate, section 10 states six contradictions with stopping conditions, section 11 tests nine rival readings, and section 13.13 records three retrospective checks that force revisions. The model states twelve conditional mechanisms (FM1-FM12), and the effort ledger traces his regimes from the V01 mastery ethic and kusoge exemption (section 3) through the V03 contested goal and hybrid (section 9), V09 change-readiness (section 56), V10 disclosure (section 66) and V11-V12 states (sections 71, 74, 82). A is not supported: the model claims no blind accuracy, section 13.1 says no prospective holdout was run, and the unique-usefulness mechanism is untested after V12. The countercase-tested, state-conditioned account exceeds a specialist interpretation, so C is not supported.

Section 3 orders V01-V11 developmental bands with sustained scene analysis, section 4 preserves a nine-row V11 state vector after the reconciliation and co-proposal (not the deepest withdrawal), and section 16.11 overlays a V12 table that keeps the V11 state historical. The model binds behavior to sixteen selectors from F01_GAME_EXPERT_SOCIAL_NOVICE to F12_PUBLIC_PURPOSE, each with a knowledge and transfer ceiling, and forbids a generic V12 state for the whole corpus; the effort ledger gives dated regime tables (sections 3-4, 9, 13, 28, 36, 38, 43-45, 47, 56-58, 64, 82) with V01-V12 hypothesis dispositions. A is not supported because coverage follows material episodes rather than every volume, the V11 acute and repair selectors are adjacent and must be supplied, and nothing after V12 is established. C would understate a phase-indexed account with explicit change controls.

The discovery row claims speech. Section 7 locates attested features: ordinary 俺, casual forms with Hinami, NO NAME or nanashi in their shared game world, Kikuchi-san and Haruka-chan as different address relations, and the modal contrast between V03 優先したい and なしにしたい (wanting and proposing about his own goal) and the V11 imperative 俺を信じろ tied to his unbeaten status. Section 7.4 separates speech from inward narration, and section 7.1 describes the hesitant entry and analytical-miniature comedy of his V01 answer about Mimimi and Tama. B is not supported: section 7.2 says twenty-four selected records cannot support an idiolect and assigns no catchphrase or particle frequency, the voice ledger is not curated on this subject, and the model performs no freeform Japanese, lexical-frequency or acoustic evaluation and returns register constraints only in analytical prose. D would ignore the located forms and their analyzed force.

Section 9 classifies ordinary evidence by strength, mainly from two primary-checked supplemental episodes: the V06.5 clothing trip (TF-P01, P1-216: earlier purchases with part-time wages, vocabulary outrunning judgment, the rear-view blind spot, price attention with savings meant for arcade play and downloadable content, clerk feedback, the observed black Chesterfield coat purchase) and the V08.5 first Christmas (TF-P02, P1-101: the small snowman, the photograph with a learned camera operation, the corrected scheduling offer). Section 16.6 adds V12 family logistics, the ferry, the descriptive word game, shared food and an awkward lodging. Section 9.7 tabulates each with its limit. B is not supported because the profile rests on a few occasions and section 9.7 abstains on food, drink, music, sleep and domestic routines. D is not supported because two sustained ordinary episodes are read at the primary level with explicit strength classes.

Section 8 gives directional accounts for Hinami (student, rival, beneficiary and would-be guarantor, with an escalation of standing as his characteristic failure), Kikuchi (three different reciprocity failures under opportunity, guilt and defeat), Mimimi (comic reciprocity, unreciprocated love and her correction of his V09 withdrawal), Tama (learner fit), Mizusawa (the peer who makes him answer for evasions), Yuzu, Nakamura and Takei, Rena (real refusals and an incomplete account to Kikuchi) and Ashigaru. Section 16 adds V12 Mizusawa (more pessimism told to him than to Kikuchi, the borrowed best-friend fiction), Mitsu and a later Hinami encounter. The model requires a named recipient and directional relationship as input, and the effort ledger separates his ownership state per relationship (sections 8, 47, 57-58, 66). A is not supported because section 8 says it does not replace the unfinished dyadic and ensemble syntheses and the relationship ledger is not curated on this subject. C would understate recipient-specific accounts with costs.

Fumiya narrates the novels in first person, and the curated items locate his inward states and keep them apart from speech: the V03 inability to complete a rational rebuttal while refusing a confession task, the unspoken 'as a person' qualification to his spoken liking of Hinami to Haruka (section 7.4, V11), his recognition of Kikuchi's hurt during the V11 call while answering from shame, his V06.5 reflection that enjoyment is a prerequisite for his game practice (ledger section 31.5), his V10 recognition that telling Mizusawa violates Hinami's right (ledger section 66), and in V12 his narrated knowledge that his own-will framing will secure Kikuchi's acceptance and is unfair (section 16.3, P96-98). A is not supported: section 1 says represented speech is not a reliable self-diagnosis and narration is not what listeners heard, and the monograph's fresh primary returns are selective windows. Located interiority across many phases exceeds C.

Located conflict across phases: the V03 station objection to an assigned confession, the overshooting withdrawal and the negotiated hybrid (ledger section 9); his V04-V05 punishment reformulation and objection to Hinami's excessive retaliation (section 3.4); pausing regular coaching in V09 over the engineered first quarrel; the V09 deletion of peer structures under guilt; the V08 tournament-format loss to Ashigaru through escape by risk and then escape by control (ledger section 45); the V11 imperative guarantee, Boxman set loss and exclusionary call; explicit refusal of Rena's sexual proposition; and the V12 costume access after Mitsu's warning, followed by owning the proposal and a narrower repair. The model's FM2, FM7, FM8, FM9 and FM11 state conditions for these branches. A is not supported because the model gives no stopping thresholds and the monograph's probes 13.6 and 13.11 give low confidence for the exact decision or words. C would understate located, countercase-bearing conduct.

Much of his own moral reasoning is narrated rather than only reconstructed: refusing a feasible confession because he does not yet know he wants the relationship (V03), the punishment reformulation of a group attack (V04-V05), refusing to choose Mimimi as consolation or debt (V07), refusing to make the couple's quarrel an exercise (V09), explicitly calling the disclosure to Mizusawa a violation of Hinami's right and proceeding because she is special (V10, ledger section 66), and acknowledging the unfairness of his own-will rhetoric (V12). Section 5.6 analyzes sincerity with an unstable account of jurisdiction, and the model's FM8, FM10 and FM11 keep usefulness and permission separate. A is not supported because section 10.1 says no complete rule for continuing care versus continuing an unauthorized method is shown, and the model says unknown stopping thresholds remain unknown. The located first-person deliberation exceeds C.

Sections 7.1 and 7.5 locate his comedy: the analytical-miniature answer that Mimimi enjoys and Tama does not (V01), the jointly produced game-analogy teasing with Hinami over clothes (V06.5), the proudly low threshold for a non-blurred Christmas photograph, the Found gesture closing the V03 argument, and the V12 word game and borrowed best-friend fiction; section 16.9 records a joking offer to replace Nagisa that he withdraws at once. The monograph says reception depends on the recipient and that a forecast should not insert game references everywhere, and the model refuses to treat every disclaimer as a symptom. B is not supported because much of the comedy is inward narration rather than his spoken play, the located scenes are few, and no frequency or validated speech exists. D would ignore sustained, recipient-conditioned analysis.

Three reviewed items: a mature monograph with independent review through V12, a root-accepted derived-use model whose administrative notice records 24 producer and 18 independent cases with a bounded semantic and selective register pass, and the effort ledger, whose curated coverage on the discovery row is V01-V02 specialist analysis although its Tomozaki sections continue through V12. B is not supported because the monograph's fresh primary returns are selective windows (V01, V03, V06.5, V08.5 and V11 in TF-P01-P03 and V12 in TF-V12-E01-E09), while its V02 and V04-V10 propositions rest on inherited readings and audit routes; the claim index, character-state, relationship, social and voice ledgers it routes to are not curated on this subject; and no blind or held-out accuracy exists. D would ignore a mature, reviewed set covering V01-V12.

Affirmative limits and failures are systematic: the V10 knowing disclosure of Hinami's private history to Mizusawa; the V11 imperative guarantee resting on his unbeaten status, the 3-2 Boxman set loss and his loss of motivation even for Atafami; the exclusionary V11 call; the V09 deletion of peer structures that Mimimi corrects; the materially incomplete account of Rena to Kikuchi; recording Tama without adequate prior consent (section 3.4); deceiving Takei in the V03 Nakamura and Yuzu operation (ledger section 12.4) and the V04 tournament plan that worked on inferred Konno motives (ledger section 16); the V08 Ashigaru loss; and in V12 the costume access after Mitsu's warning and festival preparation left to Ashigaru. Each is located and bounded. A is not supported because several limits are stated as untested durability (the unique-usefulness threat after V12, future contact rules with Rena) rather than shown. C would understate the record.

The V06.5 shopping unit is placed early in the second term rather than after V06, and the V08.5 Christmas between V07 and V08 rather than as repair after V08-V09; the V11 state is preserved and V12 is an overlay; the V10/V11 school-year conflict over Nagisa stays unresolved; Hinami's V06 individual win, the V08 tournament-format loss to Ashigaru, the V11 fourth place with Jack and the V11 3-2 set stay distinct (ledger section 78.2, EFFORT-H08); and the model separates the V11 acute aftermath from the later apology and proposal. A is not supported because coverage follows material episodes, the mixed-person V11 retrospective and V12 Hinami chapter are reader access, and nothing after V12 is established. C would understate this two-clock discipline.

known_limits.statement: In V10 he told Mizusawa Hinami's private gaming and coaching history while recognizing it was not his to share and calling it a violation of her right; benevolent intent and Mizusawa's trust do not supply her permission.

In V11 he told Hinami to believe him (俺を信じろ) because she could not beat him; she won the Boxman set 3-2, which was not her first individual game win (V06), and his motivation collapsed even for Atafami.
During the V11 call he recognized Kikuchi's hurt and answered from shame and defensiveness; the call ended after she said her words were not reaching him, and the text does not say who disconnected.
In V09 he left group chats, removed a shared symbol and cancelled social participation without checking whether Kikuchi wanted that; Mimimi's correction, not his own revision, interrupted it.
He explicitly refused Rena's sexual proposition and unwanted touch, but gave Kikuchi a materially incomplete account of the contact; no durable contact rule is shown.

His spoken yes to Haruka about liking Hinami did not include his inward 'as a person' qualification, and his V11 inward remorse during the call was not heard by Kikuchi; narration is not what listeners received.

The V11 mixed-person family retrospective and Hinami's V12 first-person chapter give the reader access he does not have; he knows only what he heard, including the V10 ride, and his own later encounter.

In V12 he proposed and opened Mitsu's costume package after her warning not to do anything extra (with Kikuchi's assent), and he and Mimimi left festival preparation that Ashigaru's performance carried; later repair and benefit do not backdate permission.
In V12 he narrates knowing that framing his help for Hinami as his own will would secure Kikuchi's acceptance, and that this is unfair; her care is not a standing allocation agreement.

The V08 tournament-format loss to Ashigaru, the V11 fourth place with Jack, the V11 3-2 set loss to Hinami and the unnarrated V12 exhibition are distinct results; none establishes permanent superiority or a viable career.
The monograph's V02 and V04-V10 propositions rest on inherited readings and audit routes rather than fresh primary returns, and its V01, V03, V06.5, V08.5, V11 and V12 returns are selective windows.

The claim index, character-state, relationship, social and voice ledgers, the integration reviews and the model's evidence and review packet are not curated on this subject, and no blind or held-out accuracy is recorded.
No idiolect, frequency distribution, acoustic performance or validated freeform Japanese exists for him.
Food, drink, music, sleep and domestic routines are not established; the located clothing selections are one episode.
Whether he can receive care or accept Hinami's refusal under another unique-usefulness threat is not tested after V12.
Career viability, the promotion and follower outcomes, the exhibition result, relationship durability and any later outcome are not established; nothing after V12 is assessed.

dimensions.note: The evidence says what changes his response. Whether he owns the end or it is assigned (V03 優先したい, FM2); the learner's own aim (Tama curriculum, FM3); whether a loss is information or a verdict on his unique standing (monograph 5.3, 10.3, FM7); whether an action stays responsive to the person or chiefly restores his sense that he can act (5.5); and urgency with special attachment, which can push help past his informational standing (FM8, 10.5). The model predicts his mistakes, not only his prudence: the V09 peer deletion on Kikuchi's presumed behalf (10.4), the knowing V10 disclosure to Mizusawa, the V11 俺を信じろ guarantee resting on his unbeaten status (7.3), the exclusionary call (5.3), the V12 costume access after Mitsu's warning, and the own-will rhetoric he narrates as unfair (16.3; ledger 82, p-0011 P97-98). Why not A: confidence is qualitative, the section 13 probes are retrospective with no prospective holdout (13.1), the model gives no stopping thresholds, and durability under another unique-usefulness threat is untested after V12 (13.11, 16.11). Why not C: the predecessor's overall C rested on these same limits. Under the owner rulings they narrow scope and confidence; the evidence does tell which mechanism governs in each located condition, so the gaps are productive uncertainty, not insufficiency.

Section 9 classifies ordinary evidence by strength, mainly from two primary-checked supplemental episodes: the V06.5 clothing trip (TF-P01: purchases with part-time wages, price attention with savings meant for arcade play and downloadable content, clerk feedback, the observed coat purchase) and the V08.5 first Christmas (TF-P02: the small snowman, the photograph, the corrected scheduling offer); section 16.6 and 16.11 add V12 family logistics, the word game, shared food and particular affection, and section 9.7 tabulates each with its restriction. Why not B: the profile rests on a few occasions and does not discriminate how he would choose across ordinary situations beyond valuing shared minor activity for its companion; section 9.7 abstains on food, drink, music, sleep and domestic routines. This is a property of the ordinary evidence, not a second count of scope limits. Why not D: two sustained ordinary episodes read at paragraph level with a tabulated preference ledger exceed listed habits.

Section 8 gives directional accounts for Hinami (student, rival, beneficiary and would-be guarantor), Kikuchi (the desired partner whose words he must allow to matter), Mimimi (comic reciprocity, unreciprocated love and her correction of his V09 withdrawal), Tama (learner fit), Mizusawa (the peer who makes him answer for evasions), Yuzu, Nakamura and Takei, Rena and Ashigaru; section 16 adds V12 Mizusawa, Mitsu and a later Hinami encounter. The model requires a named recipient and directional relationship as input, and the ledger separates his ownership state per relationship. Why not A: section 8 does not replace the unfinished relationship specialists, and the Hinami priority is deliberately left without a romantic classification. Why not C: differentiated, directional responses across many attested recipients exceed a relational sketch.

He narrates the novels in first person, and the curated items locate his inward states and keep them apart from speech: the V03 inability to complete a rational rebuttal while refusing a confession task, the unspoken 'as a person' qualification to his spoken liking of Hinami to Haruka (5.4, 7.4), his recognition of Kikuchi's hurt during the V11 call while answering from shame, his V10 recognition that telling Mizusawa violates Hinami's right, and his V12 narrated knowledge that his own-will framing will secure Kikuchi's acceptance and is unfair (16.3; ledger 82). Why not A: represented narration is not a reliable self-diagnosis, and the monograph's fresh primary returns are selective windows. Why not C: sustained, located first-person access separated from speech exceeds inference from conduct.

Located conflict across phases with conditions: the V03 station objection, overshooting withdrawal and negotiated hybrid; the V04-V05 objection to excessive retaliation; the V09 deletion of peer structures under guilt; the V11 imperative guarantee, set loss and exclusionary call; the explicit refusal of Rena's proposition; and the V12 costume access after Mitsu's warning, followed by owning the proposal. The model's FM2, FM7, FM8, FM9 and FM11 state when each branch is live, and section 10 states the stopping conditions the corpus does and does not show. Why not A: the model gives no stopping thresholds, and probe 13.11 rates acute vulnerability moderate and duration low. Why not C: mechanism-level treatment of many located conflicts exceeds incidents alone.

Much of his moral reasoning is narrated: refusing a feasible confession because he does not yet know he wants the relationship (V03), refusing to choose Mimimi as consolation or debt (V07), refusing to make the couple's quarrel an exercise (V09), calling the disclosure to Mizusawa a violation of Hinami's right and proceeding because she is special (V10), and acknowledging the unfairness of his own-will rhetoric (V12). Section 5.6 analyzes sincerity with an unstable account of jurisdiction, and FM8, FM10 and FM11 keep usefulness and permission separate. Why not A: section 10.1 says no complete rule for continuing care versus continuing an unauthorized method is shown. Why not C: weighed reasons in his own narration across five phases exceed positions alone.

Sections 7.1 and 7.5 locate his comedy: the analytical-miniature answer about Mimimi and Tama (V01), game-analogy teasing with Hinami over clothes (V06.5), the low threshold for a non-blurred Christmas photograph, and the V12 word game and borrowed best-friend fiction; section 2 says familiarity releases more teasing and improvisation, and the model refuses to treat every disclaimer as a symptom. Why not B: much of the comedy is inward narration rather than spoken play, the located scenes are few, and the evidence does not say what triggers or suppresses play beyond familiarity. Why not D: recipient-conditioned analysis across several phases exceeds a single mention.

Three reviewed items: a mature monograph with independent review through V12, a root-accepted derived-use model, and the effort ledger, whose curated coverage now runs through V12 in its specialist domain. Why not B: the monograph's fresh primary returns are selective windows (V01, V03, V06.5, V08.5 and V11 in TF-P01-P03 and V12 in TF-V12-E01-E09), its V02 and V04-V10 propositions rest on inherited readings and audit routes, the ledger covers its specialist domain rather than a general model, and the claim index and the character-state, relationship, social and voice ledgers are not curated on this subject. Why not D: a mature, reviewed set covering V01-V12 exceeds limited local evidence.

Affirmative limits and failures are systematic and located: the V10 knowing disclosure of Hinami's private history to Mizusawa; the V11 guarantee, the 3-2 Boxman set loss and his loss of motivation even for Atafami; the exclusionary V11 call; the V09 peer deletion Mimimi corrects; the incomplete account of Rena to Kikuchi; the V08 Ashigaru loss; and in V12 the costume access after Mitsu's warning and the council preparation left to Ashigaru (16.10; ledger 82, p-0026 P181). Section 13.13 records three retrospective checks that forced model revisions. Why not A: several limits are untested durability rather than tests (the unique-usefulness threat after V12, future contact rules). Why not C: located failures with explicit countercases exceed bare gap statements.

The V06.5 shopping unit is placed early in the second term and the V08.5 Christmas between V07 and V08 rather than as repair after V08-V09; the V11 state is preserved and V12 is an overlay; the model separates the V11 acute aftermath from the later repair proposal; the V08 tournament-format loss to Ashigaru, the V11 fourth place, the V11 3-2 set and the unnarrated V12 exhibition stay distinct; and the ledger keeps sections 1-78 at their dated boundaries with sections 79-84 as the latest state. Why not A: coverage follows material episodes, and the mixed-person V11 retrospective and V12 Hinami chapter are reader access. Why not C: this two-clock discipline exceeds a loose period.

known_limits.statement: In V10 he told Mizusawa Hinami's private gaming and coaching history while recognizing it was not his to share and calling it a violation of her right; benevolent intent and Mizusawa's trust do not supply her permission.

In V11 he told Hinami to believe him (俺を信じろ) because she could not beat him; she won the Boxman set 3-2, which was not her first individual game win (V06), and his motivation collapsed even for Atafami.
During the V11 call he recognized Kikuchi's hurt and answered from shame and defensiveness; the call ended after she said her words were not reaching him, and the text does not say who disconnected.
In V09 he left group chats, removed a shared symbol and cancelled social participation without checking whether Kikuchi wanted that; Mimimi's correction, not his own revision, interrupted it.
He explicitly refused Rena's sexual proposition and unwanted touch, but gave Kikuchi a materially incomplete account of the contact; no durable contact rule is shown.

His spoken yes to Haruka about liking Hinami did not include his inward 'as a person' qualification, and his V11 inward remorse during the call was not heard by Kikuchi; narration is not what listeners received.

The V11 mixed-person family retrospective and Hinami's V12 first-person chapter give the reader access he does not have; he knows only what he heard, including the V10 ride, and his own later encounter.

In V12 he proposed and opened Mitsu's costume package after her warning not to do anything extra (with Kikuchi's assent), and he and Mimimi left council preparation that Ashigaru's performance carried; later repair and benefit do not backdate permission or pay that cost.
In V12 he narrates knowing that framing his help for Hinami as his own will would secure Kikuchi's acceptance, and that this is unfair; her care is not a standing allocation agreement.

The V08 tournament-format loss to Ashigaru, the V11 fourth place, the V11 3-2 set loss to Hinami and the unnarrated V12 exhibition are distinct results; none establishes permanent superiority or a viable career.

The model performs no freeform Japanese dialogue, lexical-frequency idiolect, acoustic or broad surface-authenticity evaluation, returns register constraints in prose, and forbids distributing a few local words as catchphrases or voicing private qualification as dialogue.
Whether he can receive care or accept Hinami's refusal under another unique-usefulness threat is untested after V12; this limits that domain rather than the record's tier.
The monograph's V02 and V04-V10 propositions rest on inherited readings and audit routes rather than fresh primary returns, and its V01, V03, V06.5, V08.5, V11 and V12 returns are selective windows.

The model derives from the monograph, so the two are one analytical line; the section 13 probes are retrospective with no prospective holdout, and the claim index, the other ledgers, the integration reviews and the model's evidence and review packet are not curated on this subject.
Food, drink, music, sleep and domestic routines are not established; the located clothing selections are one episode.
Career viability, the promotion and follower outcomes, the exhibition result, relationship durability and any later outcome are not established; nothing after V12 is assessed.
